title: HighDimensionalEllSmoothNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a possibly nonconvex function f on Euclidean ℝᵈ. The initial gap satisfies f(x₀) − inf f ≤ Δ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query at x returns the exact Euclidean gradient ∇f(x) together with f(x), independently of the history and oracle seed. All parameters (d, ℓ, ρ, Δ, ε, x₀) are public. The objective f is the hidden instance.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/EllSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.Reply and spec.admissible

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same oracle call returns the exact scalar f(x) at no additional query cost.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient exists and is differentiable everywhere, with ‖D∇f(x)‖op ≤ ℓ(‖∇f(x)‖). The profile ℓ is nondecreasing on [0,∞), ℓ(0)>0, and ℓ(u)/u^ρ is nonincreasing for u>0, with 0≤ρ<2.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/EllSmoothNonconvex.lean, Regular, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalEllSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The space is Euclidean ℝᵈ. For K=(2−ρ)Δℓ(ε)/(2²⁷ε²), validity requires ε>0, K≥1 and d≥2⁵⁶(⌊K⌋+1)⁶(ℓ(ε)/ℓ(0))⁴.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The criterion uses the Euclidean gradient norm to the first power at the single returned point X. X may be any point computed from the algorithm state, including a point that was never queried.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/EllSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.Output and spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.output and _run

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: X must be measurable, ‖∇f(X)‖ must be integrable, and E[‖∇f(X)‖]≤ε. The algorithm may randomize despite the exact oracle replies.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/EllSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.successful and spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.Seed, Algorithm.law and Setup.allowedAlgorithm

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The curvature bound depends on the gradient norm through a public function ℓ with a subquadratic growth restriction. The admissible dimension threshold also depends on the ratio ℓ(ε)/ℓ(0) and the initial gap.

descriptionHtml:
High-Dimensional ℓ-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization

We seek an approximate stationary point of a possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R in high dimension d. Its Hessian exists everywhere and has operator norm bounded by ℓ(∥∇f(x)∥) at each point x, where ℓ:R→R is positive and nondecreasing on [0,∞) with subquadratic growth. A given starting point x0∈Rd has objective value within Δ≥0 of the infimum. The oracle returns (f(x),∇f(x)) at x. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈Rd with E[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness.

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). We use the Euclidean norm ∥⋅∥ and its induced operator norm ∥⋅∥op. The algorithm receives d, ℓ, the growth exponent ρ∈[0,2), Δ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness profile). For 0≤u≤v, the profile satisfies 0<ℓ(u)≤ℓ(v). Its growth on positive arguments satisfies ℓ(v)vρ≤ℓ(u)uρ,0<u≤v.

Assumption 2 (Curvature and initial gap). The function f and its gradient are Fréchet differentiable everywhere. For every x∈Rd, ∥∇2f(x)∥op≤ℓ(∥∇f(x)∥),f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Accuracy and dimension regime). Let s=(2−ρ)Δℓ(ε)/(227ε2). The tolerance and the dimension d∈N satisfy s≥1,d≥256(⌊s⌋+1)6(ℓ(ε)ℓ(0))4.

Queries may be made at any point of Rd. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, and its gradient norm must be integrable and satisfy E[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Yanpeng Liang and Luo Luo. On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic (L0,L1)-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization. 2026, arXiv v1. Complexity: Ω(A+B) exact-gradient oracle calls for randomized methods to attain E∥∇f(X)∥≤ε in the zero-noise case, where ℓ(u)=L0+L1u, A=L0Δ/ε2, and B=L1Δ/ε. The regime is L0,L1>0 and ε≤cmin{L0Δ,L1Δ} for a universal c>0. A sufficient dimension is d≳max{A2log⁡(2+A),Br2log2⁡(er)log⁡(2+B)} with r=max{1,L1ε/L0}.
theorems.formulaHtml: ⌊(2−ρ)⋅Δ⋅ℓ(ε)227⋅ε2⌋+

comparisonHtml:
The objective f:Rd→R is twice differentiable with f(x0)−inff≤Δ and ∥∇2f(x)∥≤ℓ(∥∇f(x)∥). The profile ℓ is nondecreasing on [0,∞), ℓ(0)>0, and ℓ(u)/uρ is nonincreasing for u>0, with 0≤ρ<2. For ε>0, assume N≥1 and d≥256(N+1)6(ℓ(ε)/ℓ(0))4. Randomized algorithms know the setup parameters and can query exact (f,∇f) anywhere. The target is E∥∇f(x^)∥≤ε over the algorithm’s seed, with measurable output and integrable gradient norm.

Derived bound via Young’s inequality for 1<ρ<2.		 Ω(L0Δε2+L1′Δε) gradient calls. Local gradient-difference condition with intercept ≍L0, slope ≍L1′. Requires ε≲L0Δ+L1′Δ. (1): For 1<ρ<2 and r≥1, the necessary-budget expressions differ by a factor of order (2−ρ)r(ρ−1)/ρ. At ρ=3/2, r=106, they are Ω(106L0Δ/ε2) and Ω(104L0Δ/ε2), respectively. Applies even with exact values. (1): Factor 2−ρ degrades near 2. More restrictive dimension requirement in the gain regime, with sixth-power dependence on N.
(3) (Carmon et al. 2020), Thm. 2, p=1.
Special case: globally L0-Lipschitz gradient.		 Ω(L0Δ/ε2) all-derivative oracle calls. Constant-probability failure implies expected-norm failure after constant rescaling of ε. (1): Extends to gradient-dependent curvature. On the power profile the necessary-budget factor is of order (2−ρ)(1+r), giving a gain when this factor is large. Matches the smooth rate at ρ=0. (1): Covers only value and gradient access. On constant profiles the dimension requirement grows as (N+1)6 versus quadratic up to a logarithm in L0Δ/ε2.

import LongTails.Setups.EllSmoothNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalEllSmoothNonconvex

open LongTails.Setups.EllSmoothNonconvex

abbrev spec : Setup := { EllSmoothNonconvex.spec with
  valid := fun (p : EllSmoothNonconvex.Params) => EllSmoothNonconvex.spec.valid p ∧ p.ρ < 2 ∧ 0 < p.ℓ 0 ∧
    2 ^ 27 * p.ε ^ 2 ≤ (2 - p.ρ) * p.Δ * p.ℓ p.ε ∧
    2 ^ 56 * ((⌊(2 - p.ρ) * p.Δ * p.ℓ p.ε / (2 ^ 27 * p.ε ^ 2)⌋₊ : ℝ) + 1) ^ 6 *
      (p.ℓ p.ε / p.ℓ 0) ^ 4 ≤ p.d }

end LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalEllSmoothNonconvex
